reports.subject: Inquiry regarding artifact reproduction results: "AXA: Cross-Language Analysis through Integration of Single-Language Analyses"
reports.content:
Dear Authors of "AXA: Cross-Language Analysis through Integration of
Single-Language Analyses"

I am Doehyun Baek, currently a PhD student at University of Stuttgart (
https://doehyunbaek.github.io/).

I am writing to you regarding the artifact for your paper, "AXA:
Cross-Language Analysis through Integration of Single-Language Analyses".
I recently attempted to reproduce the results using the artifact provided
on (https://zenodo.org/records/13374578).
While I was able to successfully run the provided tools and scripts, I
observed a minor discrepancy between the results generated by the artifact
and the values reported in Table 1 of the paper.
Below is a summary of the differences I found:
- For Row JavaScript Column Lattice, the paper says 90+14 but the artifact
says 90+1

To rerun the reproduction, you can run the following bash script:

```bash
curl
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/doehyunbaek/48ffc43dd3c7e53d23167b16319e6ebe/raw/1b6db0d988a0a6f102b9d9ae528317b7033d69f0/report_axa.sh
| bash
```

I suspect this discrepancy may be due to a transcription error when
manually transferring the artifact results into the paper.
Could you please confirm whether this interpretation is correct, or let me
know if I might be overlooking something?

Thank you for your time and for making your artifact available to the
community.

Best regards,
Doehyun Baek

Dear Authors of "A Study on the Pythonic Functional Constructs'
Understandability"

I am Doehyun Baek, currently a PhD student at University of Stuttgart (
https://doehyunbaek.github.io/).

I am writing to you regarding the artifact for your paper, "A Study on the
Pythonic Functional Constructs' Understandability".
I recently attempted to reproduce the results using the artifact provided
on  (https://zenodo.org/records/10554377).
While I was able to successfully run the provided tools and scripts, I
observed a minor discrepancy between the results generated by the artifact
and the values reported in *Table 3* of the paper.
Below is a summary of the differences I found:
- For Row Approvals Column Pr(>|z|), the paper says 0.14 but the artifact
says 0.24286.

To rerun the reproduction, you can run the following bash script:

```bash
curl
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/doehyunbaek/46d3efae2f295b731f14fd1f1c3a8a61/raw/28ceea42c7e06be3dc2ca07bff46a241b2d369a8/report_pythonic.sh
| bash
```

I suspect this discrepancy may be due to a transcription error when
manually transferring the artifact results into the paper.
Could you please confirm whether this interpretation is correct, or let me
know if I might be overlooking something?

Thank you for your time and for making your artifact available to the
community.

Best regards,

Doehyun Baek

reports.content:
Dear Authors of "Demystifying Compiler Unstable Feature Usage and Impacts
in the Rust Ecosystem"

I am Doehyun Baek, currently a PhD student at University of Stuttgart (
https://doehyunbaek.github.io/).

I am writing to you regarding the artifact for your paper, "Demystifying
Compiler Unstable Feature Usage and Impacts in the Rust Ecosystem".
I recently attempted to reproduce the results using the artifact provided
on (https://zenodo.org/records/10496086).
While I was able to successfully run the provided tools and scripts, I
observed a minor discrepancy between the results generated by the artifact
and the values reported in Table 1 of the paper.

Below is a summary of the differences I found:
- For Random Dataset, the value for Recall is 98.88% in the paper but
98.930% in the artifact.
- For Random Dataset, the value for F1 Score is 99.32% in the paper but
99.345% in the artifact.
- For Mostdep Dataset, the value for Recall is 97.47% in the paper but
97.489% in the artifact.

To rerun the reproduction, you can run the following bash script:

```bash
curl
https://gist.githubusercontent.com/doehyunbaek/3c7df54b0084e15f8224555c10122c9a/raw/63b7b2bac62775f8172eb20f602f981adf07ca26/report_rust.sh
| bash
```

I suspect this discrepancy may be due to a transcription error when
manually transferring the artifact results into the paper.
Could you please confirm whether this interpretation is correct, or let me
know if I might be overlooking something?

Thank you for your time and for making your artifact available to the
community.

Best regards,

Doehyun Baek

confirmations.subject: Re: Confirmations on the inconsistencies of Github Actions Study
confirmations.content:
If I recall correctly, some numbers became outdated during a major revision (e.g., after splitting the data into two categories) and were not fully updated (forgot to update some cells in the tables).
Other numbers were likely incorrect because they depended on those outdated values.
Additionally, at the time of writing, the scripts did not output organized tables, which led to copy-paste errors that I only noticed when re-running the full artifact.
As for the dataset differences, I do not believe the data itself was changed, but I cannot be certain: the server was cleaned at one point and the data was lost.
Although I had a copy, rewriting and updating the local scripts (which were not up to date with the ones on the server) may have fixed earlier issues (or introduced new ones), resulting in different outputs.

So in short terms:

- copy-paste mistakes
- outdated values from before major revision
- updates/refactoring of the scripts (normalizing precision, reducing dependence on hard-coded values...)

That's what I remember at this point (if I recall something else, I would follow-up by email).

Hi Doehyun,

apologies for the delay.
I had to trade time for this with many other things, like our own ISSTA submission.
I wish you good luck with yours!

The artifact is correct and the number in the paper is incorrect.
I have tried to understand how the wrong number entered the table, but I can only guess.
The commit history says Florian has entered it along with a bigger update of numbers as we proceeded with our data analysis.
I am not sure if Florian is available to look into it right now and if he can reproduce the incorrect number for root cause analysis.
@Florian: In case you do have time to look into it, please let us know.

The takeaway for me is: Keep *all* data analyses mechanized in the repository.
There should be no single number in the paper that cannot be traced back to raw data via the artifact.
This may not have prevented the incorrect number from getting into the paper, but we would now understand why it is there and could learn from that error.

I will look into options to update the paper after the ISSTA deadline.
Not that I ever hoped for this, but finally an opportunity to explore if/how Crossmark can be utilized...

Best,
Stefan
